Class ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter

java.lang.Object
org.springframework.web.filter.GenericFilterBean
org.springframework.web.filter.OncePerRequestFilter
org.springframework.security.web.authentication.AuthenticationFilter
org.jwcarman.who.apikey.ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter
All Implemented Interfaces:
jakarta.servlet.Filter, org.springframework.beans.factory.Aware, org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanNameAware, org.springframework.beans.factory.DisposableBean, org.springframework.beans.factory.InitializingBean, org.springframework.context.EnvironmentAware, org.springframework.core.env.EnvironmentCapable, org.springframework.web.context.ServletContextAware
public final class ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter extends org.springframework.security.web.authentication.AuthenticationFilter
Signs in requests that carry an API key header, through Spring Security's AuthenticationFilter: ApiKeyAuthenticationConverter reads the header and ApiKeyAuthenticationProvider resolves the key.
  • No header, a blank one, or a request that is already authenticated (other than anonymously): the request goes on as it is.
  • A key that signs in: the request is authenticated as the key's identity, for this request only (no session is created to hold it), and goes on. As with every Spring AuthenticationFilter, a session the request already has gets a new id (on a WhoSecurity.stateless() chain, which hides the session, none does). An error page the request is forwarded to sees the same sign-in; the key is not checked again.
  • A key that does not sign in (unknown, revoked, or of an inactive identity): the request is refused at once with 401, even where anonymous access is permitted. The refusal is handed to the application as a SignInFailedException, the same answer every who sign-in gives, which never says why.

Add it to a chain with WhoApiKeySecurity, which also gives it the application's authentication event publisher, observation and exception handoff; it is not registered with the servlet container on its own.

    • doFilterInternal

      protected void doFilterInternal(jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletRequest request, jakarta.servlet.http.HttpServletResponse response, jakarta.servlet.FilterChain filterChain) throws jakarta.servlet.ServletException, IOException
      Signs the request in on its first dispatch. A later dispatch of the same request (an error page, or async processing) carries the same header, but signs in no one: it restores the sign-in the first dispatch made, if any, since the chain's own repository may not hold it (a session-backed one never does). So a key is checked, and its event published, once per request.
